questions: Can a bucket be used to extract water from multiple wells in a single lowering, or must each lowering be dedicated to a single well?
If a bucket can extract from multiple wells in one lowering, can it partially fill from one well and then continue to another in the same trip?
Is the bucket lowered exactly once per well per trip, or can it be lowered multiple times per well per trip if capacity allows?
Does the bucket need to be fully filled to capacity on each lowering, or can it be partially filled?
Are there any constraints on the order in which wells are emptied or bucket lowerings are performed?
Should the output be an integer, and if so, is rounding always up as per the reference solution?
What if capacity is zero? Is that a valid input?
Is the grid guaranteed to be non-empty?
answers: Each lowering is dedicated to a single well, as the reference solution sums per well.
Not applicable because each lowering is per well.
It can be lowered multiple times per well as needed, with the number of lowerings per well being ceil(water in well / capacity).
It can be partially filled on the final lowering for a well if the remaining water is less than capacity.
No constraints on order; the total lowerings is independent of sequence.
Yes, the output is an integer, and rounding is always up per well.
Capacity is at least 1 per constraints, so zero is not a valid input.
Yes, grid length is at least 1 per constraints.
